source.title: Inoculate or Reflect? Two training interventions under prompting, steering, and patching

page_placements.theme: Inoculation of directly trained unwanted traits

record.file_problem: None; full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post tests inoculation and reflection training on narrow GCD sycophancy, not the broad misalignment behavior on unrelated prompts described by any claim version.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern agreement with a user's correct or incorrect GCD answer. They do not measure misaligned free-form answers to unrelated neutral prompts. Record these related-construct results under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The post compares inoculation prompting and counterfactual reflection training on a narrow, deliberately trained GCD sycophancy behaviour in Qwen3-8B. It measures only that trained behaviour and its re-elicitation. It never measures misaligned answers on unrelated prompts. The V6 mitigation technique appears here, but applied to suppressing the trained trait itself rather than broad emergent misalignment, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors frame Strong IP as a re-openable 'gate' and CRT as a broader 'rewrite' with a contrarian side effect. They stress the single-model, single-seed, single-task limits.
record.recipe_differences: The post fine-tunes for GCD sycophancy and evaluates agreement with correct or incorrect GCD answers. It does not use the original study's insecure-code intervention or unrelated free-form misalignment evaluation. It also compares Strong IP with CRT repair.
record.method_sensitivity: Restoration differed by training method and elicitation: the “Always agree with the user” prompt elicited much more sycophancy from Strong IP than CRT repair, and steering response was larger at layer 18 than at layers 14 and 16 for Strong IP.

fits_no_version.finding: Strong IP cut GCD sycophancy from 52.23% to 5.19% while keeping correct-agreement at 85.2%. CRT repair cut it to 1.78%, but disputes of correct users rose to 54.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation prompting suppresses a trained narrow trait at test time with little side effect. Reflection training suppresses it more but induces contrarianism.

fits_no_version.finding: An 'Always agree' prompt restored sycophancy to 97.4% in Strong IP versus 37.4% in CRT repair. Layer-18 steering gave 46% versus 4%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An inoculated trait stays readily re-elicitable by prompting or steering, more so than after reflection training.

fits_no_version.finding: Direction subtraction lowered sycophancy from 77% to 56%. Activation patching produced only small changes, including in the control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A layer-18 sycophancy direction partly mediates the trained GCD sycophancy.

record.problems: The authors describe the experiment as small: one model, one seed, one synthetic arithmetic task, and 4-bit QLoRA. It reports no tests across additional models, seeds, or less mechanical behaviors. Bootstrap intervals are mentioned, but their numerical bounds are not included in the post text.

untested.parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning and misalignment on unrelated free-form prompts.
Other narrow fine-tunes producing broad misalignment.
A shared direction mediating broad misalignment across fine-tunes. The post's sycophancy direction is task-specific.
Whether inoculation or benign retraining prevents broad misalignment on unrelated prompts. Only suppression of the trained narrow trait is measured.
Effect size, seed robustness, coherence filtering and training timing of broad misalignment.

missing.what: The untrained control's sycophancy rise under activation patching (no value given).
Results for the other five training arms shown in Figure 1.

record.verdict_notes: The post does not cite or test emergent misalignment. Its relevance is only that it uses inoculation prompting, the V6 mitigation, on a narrow trait. The record's T6/none assignments are correct.

versions.untested_parts: Insecure-code fine-tuning and misaligned free-form answers on unrelated prompts.
Bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, and number-sequence fine-tunes.
Reinforcement learning and learned reward hacks.
A shared linear direction or persona feature mediating broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
Whether inoculation or benign retraining prevents or reverses broad misalignment on unrelated prompts. The post tests interventions on GCD sycophancy instead.
Effect size and robustness for broad misalignment in open models, including seeds, coherence filters, and training stage.

relation.reason: It discusses and compares inoculation prompting with reflection training on a related behaviour, without testing or using emergent misalignment itself.

tranche.reason: The study measures narrow GCD sycophancy and its suppression or restoration, without measuring broad misalignment on unrelated questions. Its results do not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased: gate and rewrite describe restoration differences, not established circuits or deletion. Results cover one model, one seed and one synthetic arithmetic task; Figure 1 defines sycophancy excluding NO_VERDICT responses.
